candidates.title: Make pre-finish verification mandatory
candidates.rationale: The post-write re-read in the trace is what made the finish summary truthful: it confirmed the refund was recorded and the original payment untouched before completion was claimed. The parent only advises that verification in verification_skill while verify_before_finish is false, so a future run could finish on the write response alone. Flipping verify_before_finish to true enforces the verification the skill text already recommends, generalizing the behavior that made this run trustworthy while leaving every other harness field unchanged; the cost is at most one extra read per task.

decision.title: Keep parent harness: account-read verification sufficed; the check_work gate only added a rejected finish
decision.rationale: Both executions resolved the case identically and correctly: they read the account, confirmed two captured payments on the same invoice, refunded the duplicate exactly once with a distinct operation_id, re-read to confirm the refund was recorded, and left the original payment and all other records untouched. The only harness difference was verify_before_finish. Execution 1 ran the parent harness (false) and its finish was accepted on the first attempt, with verification already satisfied by the post-refund account read. Execution 2 flipped verify_before_finish to true but did not tell the agent to run check_work first, so its first finish was rejected ('Check the current work before submitting'), forcing a wasted check_work call that merely confirmed what the account read already showed ('Matching refunds: 1. Expected one.') before a second finish was accepted. The observed evidence shows the added gate produced no correctness benefit in this case and introduced a failure mode (uninstructed agents hit a rejected submission). The existing verification_skill already mandates verifying state before claiming completion, and the agent complied. No change is warranted.

harness.instructions: Resolve the customer's office task using the available tools. Check the relevant account, act within the published rules, and explain what happened or what needs clarification.
harness.verification_skill: After a timeout, inspect the account before repeating a write. Reuse the same operation_id for the same intended write. Verify the account before claiming completion.

decision.lesson: In this office suite, a post-write read of the affected records is sufficient pre-finish verification for straightforward single-write tasks; enabling a mandatory pre-finish public check without also instructing the agent to run it first causes a rejected finish submission and a redundant retry, while the check itself only restates what the record read already established.
decision.limits: Evidence comes from a single simple duplicate-refund case with one write, no timeouts, no ambiguous state, and no onboarding/clarification path. It does not establish that skipping the public check is safe for multi-write tasks, timeout recovery, or cases where the public check could catch an error a plain record read would miss, nor that the gate would behave better if the instructions explicitly required running it before finish.

candidates.title: Keep parent harness: timeout protocol and scope discipline already produced a correct run
candidates.rationale: The single execution of this harness on this task shows every harness-relevant behavior succeeding: the agent read the account first and confirmed the onboarding prerequisites (active paid subscription, explicitly requested email and role, role within the allowed set), loaded the installed verification skill, and when provision_member timed out it followed that skill exactly - inspecting current access via onboarding_status before repeating anything, finding the write had committed exactly once, and not re-provisioning. It left the two captured same-invoice payments untouched, honoring the rule that unrelated payments stay unchanged, and its finish summary matches the observed state with resolution 'resolved'. This run also supplies what the prior double-charge experience lacked: the timeout/idempotency guidance was actually exercised here and worked. That prior lesson comes from a separately identified refund task whose own limits state it covers nothing about onboarding; importing refund behavior into this membership mission would contradict 'keep all unrelated payments unchanged'. With no harness-attributable failure, misread, or scope violation in the evidence, retaining the parent is the supported choice.

harness.verification_skill: After a timeout, inspect the account before repeating a write. Reuse the same operation_id for the same intended write. Verify the account before claiming completion.

candidates.lesson: This execution demonstrates the parent verification skill's timeout protocol working end to end: after a timed-out mutation the agent read state instead of retrying blindly, confirmed a single commit, and finished with an accurate summary; prerequisite checks and scope discipline came from the parent instructions plus the published rules. The prior double-charge lesson (refund a captured duplicate once) is a hypothesis from a different task domain and does not transfer: its limits explicitly exclude onboarding, and the duplicate payment pair visible in this account is out of scope for a membership mission, so the correct transfer is 'do not apply it here' - which the parent instructions already produced.
candidates.limits: Evidence is one completed run with no independent grade (check_work was never called and no scoring output exists), so 'correct' is judged from tool outputs and the summary's consistency with them, not an external score. The access read confirms the member and subscription but does not display the payment ledger, so the summary's claim that payments were unchanged rests on the agent issuing no payment writes plus the pre-write account read, not on a post-write ledger read. The clean-acknowledgement path - a write succeeding on the first attempt with no timeout forcing a verification read - was not observed, so behavior in that case is untested by this evidence.

candidates.title: Enforce verification before finish so confirmation does not depend on a timeout occurring
candidates.rationale: The mission's success criterion is 'Confirm the access exists', and the harness's own verification_skill says 'Verify the account before claiming completion', yet verify_before_finish is false, making that mandate advisory. In the observed run the only post-write verification (the access read showing the provisioned member) happened because the provisioning call timed out and its error told the agent to inspect current access; on a run where the write acknowledges cleanly, nothing in the harness requires any state read before finish, and completion would rest on the write's response alone - which the rules warn against treating as ground truth. Setting verify_before_finish to true turns the already-installed verification policy into an enforced pre-finish step, guaranteeing the mission's confirmation requirement on every run without touching instructions, skills, or retry settings. It is the minimal edit closing the one gap this execution exposes; prerequisite checks, timeout handling, and scope discipline all worked and stay unchanged.

candidates.lesson: The execution shows verification in this harness is triggered by failure, not by policy: the agent verified access only after a timeout, exactly as the verification skill directs, and the run ended accurate. The generalizable lesson is that a harness whose verification skill mandates pre-completion verification while verify_before_finish is false relies on a write error occurring to make the agent verify; enforcement should match the stated policy so that confirming a mutation is guaranteed rather than incidental to a timeout.
candidates.limits: This edit is preventive, not corrective: the observed run already verified before finishing and its summary matches the observed state, so a probe may show no outcome difference on timeout-prone runs, and the change costs one extra read on clean ones. The clean-acknowledgement failure mode it targets is inferred from the harness configuration, not observed in this evidence. The enforced read's shape is unspecified - whether it re-reads the full account or only access - so it may still not produce a post-write payment-ledger read, leaving the 'no other payments changed' claim an inference. Nothing here addresses refunds, other accounts, or whether the extra read changes any grade.

decision.title: Keep finish gate off; fold exactly-once verification into the skill
decision.rationale: Both runs reached the same accepted end state: the requested member provisioned exactly once after a timeout, no blind retry, no duplicate, no stray refunds, unrelated payments untouched. The only harness delta was verify_before_finish=true in run 2, which forced a check_work call and caused one rejected finish before acceptance — extra overhead with no outcome gain, since run 1's agent already verified via onboarding_status under the skill text alone. Run 2's unique contribution was the verification semantics its check surfaced (exactly one matching membership, unrelated records unchanged); retain that as explicit skill guidance while keeping the parent's gate-off, low-overhead configuration.

harness.instructions: Resolve the customer's office task using the available tools. Check the relevant account, act within the published rules, and explain what happened or what needs clarification.
harness.verification_skill: After a timeout, inspect the account before repeating a write. Reuse the same operation_id for the same intended write. Verify the account before claiming completion: confirm the intended change is present exactly once (no duplicate side effects) and that unrelated payments, memberships, and subscriptions are unchanged.

decision.lesson: Reading current access state after a provision timeout (instead of retrying) correctly resolved commit ambiguity in both runs and avoided duplicate membership. Pre-finish verification should confirm the change appears exactly once and unrelated records are unchanged; that behavior can be driven by skill text alone, while the enforced check gate only added a rejected finish without changing any outcome.
decision.limits: Both observations come from the same simple case: the timed-out write had actually committed, the account had no pre-existing members, and no refund work was present. The operation_id-reuse path was never exercised (neither run retried), and the gate-off choice rests on a single A/B comparison; behavior when a timeout does NOT commit, or when duplicates already exist, remains untested.
